analysis.evidence: מִלְחָמָה means “war” and is the object of עָשׂוּ. Together they mean “they waged war.” The kings listed after אֶת are their opponents.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: עָשׂוּ מִלְחָמָה means “they waged war.” The verse names Bera of Sodom and the other kings as their opponents. This rules out the source gloss “underworld.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no attached prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עָשׂוּ מִלְחָמָה אֶת בֶּרַע, the kings waged war against Bera. The parallel וְאֶת בִּרְשַׁע names Birsha as another opponent.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69121:3, 69121:6, 69121:9, 69121:12.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: The verse calls Bera מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “king of Sodom,” just as it calls Birsha מֶלֶךְ עֲמֹרָה, “king of Gomorrah.” Both names identify the cities their kings ruled.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “king of Sodom.”
